public_configuration.snapshot_batch_aliases: preassigned opaque aliases, not content hashes or private row counts

private_input.roster: N distinct stable 32-byte user tokens; fixed even when a user has no records; encrypted under StateVault
private_input.records: arbitrary finite list of (user token, bucket code); zero denotes ineligible

compiler.histogram_slot: min of positive codes for that user, or zero when no eligible records
compiler.error: generic private rejection for unknown user, malformed record or invalid code; no raw input in exception

adjacency_argument: Fix roster, rule, catalog and all public parameters across neighboring inputs.
Neighbors differ by all records of one roster user, not by removing the user from the roster.
For any other user v, records belonging to v and its stable slot are unchanged. Its chosen bucket is therefore unchanged.
The removed user changes at most one slot from bucket j to zero. Exact count changes by at most one; exact histogram changes in at most coordinate j by one.
The existing scalar/vector mechanism bounds therefore apply separately conditional on their existing ideal-randomness and observation assumptions.
Releasing both separately perturbed count and histogram requires two charged operations. The combined exact query has L1 sensitivity two; the compiler does not make the pair a single-cost release.
Replacing a present user record set can move between two buckets, giving L1 distance two. The add/remove one-user bound must not be silently reused for replacement adjacency.
Across snapshots delete the same user records at every time, preserve the same roster identity and account lineage, and compose all operations in the existing shared accounts.

durability.atomic_pair: count ciphertext, histogram ciphertext, catalog binding and batch provenance in one transaction
durability.authority_order: whole-state witness accepts before local commit; unknown outcome freezes replica until explicit recovery
durability.ingestion_retry: duplicate batch rejected; restore and privileged audit resolve unknown outcome without recompiling or choosing new aliases
durability.crash_scope: six actual reference-process exits; no power-loss or distributed witness claim

enforcement.reservation: requires immutable batch provenance using only public metadata; no roster or snapshot decryption at query admission
enforcement.snapshot_binding: signed action pins domain/snapshot/catalog; local immutable registry and witnessed state resolve that to batch and fixed contribution rule; no new transferable ingestion signature
enforcement.lineage: same tenant and lineage cannot rebind to another domain within this database; new aliases/snapshots reuse original accounts
enforcement.audit: all snapshots covered exactly once by a paired batch; private audit checks roster and view consistency; recovery runs it before commit
enforcement.admin: direct SQL and explicit base-class method calls are privileged; Python is not an isolation boundary

negative_controls: two aliases for one human permit two contributions
count and histogram jointly have sensitivity two
new invented lineage bypasses within-database lineage uniqueness under malicious admin
